subject: Human Evolution
title: Walking and the Brain
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Walking and the Brain.

hook.text: A 20-minute walk boosts memory, creativity, and mood. Why would moving your legs change your brain?

buildup.text: Walking increases blood flow to the brain and triggers release of BDNF, a protein that grows new neurons.

discovery.text: Our brains evolved during an era of constant movement. They expect walking as a baseline input.

twist.text: Stanford found that walking boosts creative output by 60%—even on a treadmill facing a blank wall.

climax.text: Bipedalism shaped the brain that now suffers when the body stops moving. Walking feeds thinking.

punchline.text: The best thinking happens on two feet.

quiz.question: How does walking affect the brain?
options: It boosts BDNF, blood flow, and creativity
